scenes.headline: How a wall can correct a robot's drift
scenes.sub: Persistent planes as landmarks in a Gaussian splat map
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Trowel! A mapping robot slowly loses its heading. Here is how a wall it saw earlier can pull it back.

scenes.text: Remember every wall as a persistent plane. When you see it again, from anywhere, the difference between old and new is your drift.
scenes.say: Remember every wall as a persistent plane. See it again, from anywhere, and the difference is your drift.

scenes.title: The pipeline, as the figure draws it

steps.say: Each frame is tracked against the splat map.
Planes are segmented, their Gaussians flattened into the wall, and each wall keeps one identity for the whole run.
When an old plane shows up again, the stored plane and the new sighting are compared.
That becomes a pose graph edge, like a loop closure, and corrected poses carry their Gaussians along.

scenes.title: The residual, as I would write it
scenes.text: e = q(plane now) - q(T x plane then)

parts.note: two normal angles and an offset, seen now
parts.say: Left: the plane seen now, two normal angles and a distance.

parts.note: three numbers: tilt, heading, one distance
parts.say: The angles pin rotation. The distance pins only one direction; sliding along the wall stays invisible.

steps.say: The one released figure: plane instances grow the map, and matched planes become structure closures.
Closures become red pose graph edges between keyframes far apart in time.

left.title: Loop closure
left.say: Loop closure fixes the whole pose, but only on a revisit.

right.title: Structure closure
items: Fixes rotation, one offset per plane

right.say: Structure closure fixes rotation and one direction per plane, from anywhere the wall is visible.

scenes.title: A toy run: error at the end
scenes.note: Toy simulation from the article, not the paper
scenes.say: In the article's toy, one re-seen wall cuts the end error from about eight metres to a third of a metre. Assume square walls when one is tilted, and it gets worse.

scenes.text: A re-seen wall fixes heading and one direction of position, if it is really flat, square and matched correctly.
